status: immutable once committed; changes require a new protocol id and re-registration
question: Starting from the frozen Phase 2A walker (theta0), does a LOCAL search in normalised parameter space, trained for robustness across initial conditions, produce a controller that (a) preserves walking (non-inferiority, margin 5 percentage points) and (b) improves it (superiority) on untouched fresh seeds? This is a refinement experiment; it cannot show discovery of a gait from scratch.

frozen_inputs.hashing: sha256 of file bytes with CRLF normalised to LF (platform independent)

controller: PhaseGaitInitController, 15 parameters (13 gait + ramp_s + start_lean), bounds INIT_BOUNDS/phasegait.BOUNDS; no FSM, no RL

parameter_space.reflection: values crossing a bound are reflected back inside (u -> fold into [0,1])

seeds.train: derived from the screen (see training_selection); frozen in results/training_set.json before any candidate optimisation

seed_policy: pilot seeds 7300-7315 are used ONLY for implementation and resource checks and are disjoint from every other role; screen: theta0 only, executed once; train: the 16 selected screen seeds (the screen outcomes of theta0 decide membership, nothing else); validation: choose among each run's top-5, the futility gate and the winner; diagnostic: post-hoc analysis only (after the final), never used for selection; final: touched once, after selection.json is committed. Consumed and excluded: phase2a_train (1000-1002), phase2a_diagnostic (2000-2009), phase2a_heldout (3000-3019), r1_train (4000-4007), r1_validation (4100-4115), r1_diagnostic (5000-5009), r1_final (6000-6029).
initial_state: torso pitch and 6 joint angles ~ N(0, 0.03 rad) from the episode seed; feet 2 mm above floor; diagnostic stress variant N(0, 0.05) on the same diagnostic seeds, never used for selection

training_selection.rule: first 8 incumbent-walking and first 8 incumbent-not-walking seeds of the screen, ascending seed order
training_selection.insufficient_class: if either class has fewer than 8 members the registered outcome is STOP (null: screen unusable); no substitute rule
training_selection.frozen_in: experiments/phase2a_r2/results/training_set.json, committed before any candidate is optimised

order: number of training seeds passing every walking gate
training_criterion.feasibility: walking_count >= W(theta0) - 1; infeasible candidates rank below all feasible ones
training_criterion.theta0_on_training_seeds: derived from the screen (identical deterministic rollouts): 0 new rollouts, recorded in training_set.json, never re-executed

S.method: non-adaptive subset perturbation of theta0 in u-space
S.assignment: candidate i: sigma = scales[i % 4], k = sizes[(i % 12) // 4]; subset = sorted rng.choice(13, k) of the gait coordinates; deltas ~ N(0, sigma) from one sequential stream default_rng(SeedSequence([rng_base, 1, rep])); reflection at bounds; ramp_s/start_lean fixed at theta0

I.method: exhaustive 7x7 grid over (ramp_s, start_lean); other 13 coordinates = theta0
I.reference_point: grid point (ramp_s 0.5, start_lean 0.0) equals theta0: marked reference, NOT executed (0 rollouts), derived from the screen; 48 candidates executed

T.method: (1+lambda)-ES with 1/5 success rule over all 15 coordinates in u-space
T.step_rule: success rate p = (# feasible offspring strictly better than the parent)/lambda; sigma *= 1.5 if p > 0.2, *= 1.5^(-1/4) if p < 0.2, unchanged if p == 0.2; clipped to the range
T.offspring: u_parent + sigma * z, z from default_rng(SeedSequence([rng_base, 3, rep])).standard_normal((generations, lambda, 15)) (outcome-independent), then reflection
T.parent_update: best strictly-better feasible offspring (lexicographic training criterion, ties: earlier index) replaces the parent; otherwise the parent stays; the initial parent is theta0 (screen-derived)

arms.not_used: sep-CMA-ES (too little information per evaluation to justify it); possible later comparison

candidate_generation.manifest_note: sha256 of every S vector (both replicates), the full I grid, the T noise tensors and theta0, rounded to 12 digits

validation.ranking: training criterion (feasible first); top-5 history positions per run
validation.incumbent: validated once on the same 64 seeds (64 rollouts)

eligibility: validated, no error, number of body-dragging seeds <= theta0's and number of non-falling seeds >= theta0's (preservation)
selection_rule: Eligible candidates ranked by (1) validation seeds passing every walking gate, (2) non-falling validation seeds, (3) mean validation fitness, higher better; ties by arm order S<I<T, replicate, candidate index. Origin plays no role; training ranks and final seeds play no part.

futility.after: replicate 1 of S and T and the I run are trained and validated
futility.rule: stop and report a null result unless some arm's best eligible validated candidate passes every walking gate on at least 5 more of the 64 validation seeds than theta0
futility.nature: pragmatic stopping heuristic, not a significance test
futility.if_proceeding: replicate 2 of S and T (training + validation), then selection of ONE winner, committed before the final evaluation

final_evaluation.conditions: identical seeds, duration, morphology and gates; each controller executed once on the 150 seeds

confirmatory_hierarchy.order: fixed sequence; each step at its full level; step 2 is tested only if step 1 succeeds

step1_noninferiority.parameter: theta = p_win - p_inc (paired risk difference of 'passes every walking gate')
step1_noninferiority.test: Tango (1998) score test for the paired risk difference with nonzero margin (creature_forge.r2_stats)
step1_noninferiority.decision_rule: non-inferior iff the Tango score statistic at the margin exceeds z(1-0.025) = 1.959964, i.e. the lower bound of the two-sided 95% Tango score interval exceeds -0.05

step2_superiority.test: exact two-sided McNemar on the paired outcomes
step2_superiority.requires: p < alpha AND winner-only successes > incumbent-only successes

confirmatory_hierarchy.if_step1_fails: superiority is not tested confirmatorily (descriptive p reported)

engineering_criterion.note: reported separately from the statistical claims

reporting: Tango non-inferiority statistic, one-sided p and 95% interval
Wilson and exact intervals per controller
basin map: P(feasible | sigma_u, k) for arm S with Wilson intervals (descriptive)
final_evaluation.caveat: arm comparisons are exploratory; only the winner-vs-theta0 hierarchy is confirmatory

diagnostic.when: after the final evaluation; post-hoc, never used to select, tune or stop

budget.counted: every MuJoCo rollout executed or started: pilot, screen, training, validation, final, diagnostics, duplicates, retries, failed jobs, reruns
budget.reference_evaluations: theta0 is executed exactly once on each of: screen (64), validation (64), final (150), diagnostic (32) and diagnostic stress (32); its training-seed performance is derived from the screen (0 rollouts); the I-grid reference point is not executed. No silent repetition.
budget.ledger: experiments/phase2a_r2/results/ledger.jsonl (append-only, hash-chained; begin entries precede physics; session_begin/session_end events feed the wall guard)

resources.wall_definition: cumulative ACTIVE time over all script sessions (ledger session events), not idle time between runs
resources.pilot: at most 100 rollouts: theta0 + 5 candidates (S index 0 of replicate 1, S index 6 of replicate 1, T generation-0 offspring 0 and 1 of replicate 1, I grid index 24) x 16 pilot seeds 7300-7315 = 96; it checks code paths (reflection at bounds, ledger, determinism between two workers) and resources only and can change nothing in this protocol

stopping_rules: any lost or errored job, memory abort, wall-clock stop or budget breach stops the run (no silent retry)
futility gate STOP and the screen insufficient-class STOP are reported as the result
the final evaluation runs once and cannot be used to revise the controller, objective, gates or stopping rule
a null or partial result is reported as such; the search is not extended automatically
